summary.description: Finds circles in the reviewed graph and keeps only those centered on main people. Orders them by their main members’ birth years; stable member keys let narration attach text without detecting circles again.
summary.input: the reviewed graph
summary.output: ordered circles with members and ties

summary.description: Matches each person named in the shared story to the name in that person’s localized record. It asks the encyclopedia only for place labels, since the corpus already supplies the stronger evidence for people.
summary.input: the composed story and localized person data
summary.output: name evidence for people and places

summary.description: Selects the people who belong in a thematic story and gives the story its narrative frame, themes, and active eras. It uses supplied people when editors have fixed the cast; otherwise it tests registry summaries, places, and events for direct fit. It also names absent people who would fill gaps.
summary.input: the person registry and story topic

summary.description: Judges each life event against the story’s theme and keeps only landmark contributions with a concrete, lasting result. Its strict threshold makes each chapter a claim about the field’s turning points, not a chronological biography.
summary.input: the selected people and life events

summary.description: Adds historical events that directly affected the people in each chapter. It favors concrete, bounded events over famous background history and leaves chapters empty when no event has a clear connection.
summary.input: the fitted chapters with their surviving events

summary.description: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into one relationship graph. Matches names to join direct ties and keeps each person’s account of a shared tie. Retains acquaintances only when they connect multiple selected people, so the graph shows bridges instead of isolated contacts.
summary.input: selected people and ego networks
summary.output: a merged network of people and bridges

summary.description: Reviews the merged network against the biographical evidence. It adds missing direct ties, corrects misleading ones, and removes links that rest on vague or indirect contact; density-sensitive guidance keeps the circles from becoming too sparse or too crowded before clustering.
summary.input: the deterministically merged graph
summary.output: a reviewed network of biographical ties

summary.description: Turns each detected circle’s ties into a title and short factual account. It keeps the circle membership with the prose, so the story preserves the same groups used to organize the network.
summary.input: the detected circles and their ties
summary.output: a title and text per circle

summary.description: Groups rated events that lie within a shared geographic area into map stops. It scores each stop from its events, gives landmark events extra weight during selection, and orders the selected stops through time. Complete-linkage clustering keeps every event in a stop close to every other event.
summary.input: located events and per-event weights
summary.output: chronological map stops with grouped events

summary.description: Rates each located event by how much its place carries the story’s theme. The map branch uses those ratings as clustering weights, so landmark places can shape the route more than incidental settings.
summary.input: the chapters and located life events

summary.description: Curates the geographic clusters into the places that carry the story’s arc. It writes a short title and factual narrative for each surviving stop, while dropping incidental or weaker groupings so the map follows meaningful turns in the story.
summary.input: the qualifying geographic clusters
summary.output: narrated map stops and discarded clusters

summary.description: Rewrites the assembled story as one top-to-bottom account, giving its prose, chronology, network, and places a shared argument and voice. It can reorder the sections and remove map stops that do not serve that account; one whole-story pass lets it judge each part against the rest.
summary.input: circle narration, map stops, and source material
summary.output: a composed meta story with curated map stops

summary.description: Derives a dark editorial style from the story’s theme, framing, and opening. It uses abstract geometry to express the shared theme, keeping the pattern from belonging to any one biography.
summary.input: the composed story's framing and opening

summary.description: Translates the meta story into the target language and writes the localized story. It reuses settled person names and event titles so the story stays aligned with the localized person data, while the translator chooses one target-language treatment for each recurring metaphor.
summary.input: the meta story and localized person data

summary.description: Tests each selected event against the reviewed article and related articles before deciding whether its sources support an event-specific background report. Writes a report, images, and citations when the material stays with that event; otherwise leaves no background.
summary.input: reviewed events, network, and Wikipedia material

summary.description: Draws one abstract emblem for each chapter from its visual concept. It carries the portrait treatment into chapter art while keeping the image free of people and places, so the concept can stand for a period without claiming a literal scene.
summary.input: chapter concepts, style, and life events
summary.output: chapter illustrations and illustrated life events

summary.description: Develops one abstract opening image for each chapter from the finished life events. It considers all chapters together so their metaphors use distinct visual forms and avoid depicting the subject, places, or historical scenes.
summary.input: the finished life events

summary.description: Selects the events that carry a person’s life story and orders them into chapters. It weighs each event against the others because significance and the boundary between life phases emerge from comparison across the whole account. It leaves a concluding account of work that persists after the life.
summary.input: the selected articles and Wikipedia material

summary.description: Writes a sourced account of each event, naming its places and people and confining prose to the moment. It grounds the account in the subject’s article and uses event-specific related articles for detail. It records Commons searches while that material remains in view.
summary.input: an event skeleton and Wikipedia material
summary.output: a researched event with sources and image searches

summary.description: Resolves each event’s modern place name to coordinates and writes them into the life events. It prefers the research’s modern name, so a historic place with a renamed successor can retain a current map location.
summary.input: historic and modern place names

summary.description: Decides the target-language form of every person name used in a biography. It favors source evidence and preserves modern names, leaving one shared glossary so linked documents keep exact cross-references.
summary.input: name evidence and biography names
summary.output: a shared glossary of localized names

summary.description: Judges Commons search results against each background report and keeps only pictures that plainly depict things the report names. It reads filenames alongside captions because captions often describe the upload, and it leaves background illustrations for the event without repeating its existing picture or a search result.
summary.input: the background reports, searches, and life events

summary.description: Searches image archives for the planned queries and for event-specific subjects. It keeps one record per picture URL and preserves the event link when a picture appears in multiple searches, so later matching can favor images tied to a named event.
summary.input: the planned searches and event searches
summary.output: deduplicated image candidates linked to events

summary.description: Scores the pooled image hits and keeps a ranked set for event matching. It penalizes memorials from captions, filenames, and categories so modern plaques and graves do not displace period images.
summary.input: every image hit the queries returned
summary.output: ranked image candidates for event matching

summary.description: Selects one verified likeness for the person and pairs only directly relevant candidate images with life events. It treats search results as leads, rejects visual stand-ins, and leaves an event unillustrated when the metadata cannot support a defensible match.
summary.input: the ranked image candidates
summary.output: a portrait and event images with captions

summary.description: Plans Commons searches for a portrait and for things named in the life events. It favors event-specific names over places or professions, and excludes commemorations that would substitute later memorials for the person’s life.
summary.input: the event skeletons

summary.description: Checks the selected portrait against the person before the pipeline writes the life story. It judges the image itself because captions can name someone who does not appear; a negative result removes the portrait.
summary.input: the selected portrait and person name

summary.description: Collects the target-language article and linked names for the person, events, and network. It tries the leading place name only when the full comma-qualified name lacks a link, so later translation can retain the qualifier while using available naming evidence.
summary.input: reviewed names, life events, and ego network

summary.description: Builds a network of the people who directly shaped the subject’s life from the verified events and Wikipedia evidence. It keeps each tie between named individuals, so institutions and broad forces remain context instead of becoming people in the story.
summary.input: the finished life events and Wikipedia material

summary.description: Redraws the licensed reference portrait in the story’s shared light-drawing style while preserving the person’s likeness. It uses the story palette and a master portrait so each person’s image belongs to the same visual set, then records the finished portrait for the person and their life events.
summary.input: the person registry and interface style
summary.output: a portrait linked to the person and events

summary.description: Reviews the life story and ego network together against the available biographical sources. It proposes high-confidence corrections that improve factual support, story continuity, prose, and links between events and people.
summary.input: the life events, ego network, and sources
summary.output: revised life events and ego network

summary.description: Derives the story’s dark-mode colors and type choices from the person’s work, materials, and depicted places. It also leaves an abstract background pattern tied to that evidence, while contrast checks keep the colors readable without washing out their source hues.
summary.input: the finished life events

summary.description: Translates the person record, life events, network, reports, and captions into the target language. It applies the name glossary and source-language naming evidence across the text. It overlays translated fields on the English record, leaving dates, coordinates, links, and identifiers unchanged.
summary.input: the person data, reports, and name mapping

summary.description: Fetches the main article, related article candidates, and image metadata for a subject. Writes a research bundle that later story steps can reuse.
summary.input: a subject or article URL
summary.output: Wikipedia research material for the subject

summary.description: Ranks linked articles for the biographical context and keeps those centered on people, life events, or personal works. It steers later research away from broad background topics that add little to the subject’s life story.
summary.input: the article and outgoing link candidates
